question.leadin: Two Hittite spies were tortured in the prelude to this battle, and one side in this battle was commanded by Muwatallis II.
question.text: Name this 1274 BCE battle in which the Ra and Ptah divisions contributed to the largest chariot battle in history.
question.clue: The opposing leader declared victory in the success of his empire's technological advances in matching those of the opposing Hittites.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about famous archaeological finds in Egypt.
swap.text: This British archaeologist led the 1922 excavation of King Tut's tomb in the Valley of the Kings, with funding from Lord Carnavon.
swap.clue: Starting at age 17, this person worked for Gaston Maspero, who provided a recommendation for a later employer.

question.text: This last pharaoh of Ancient Egypt unsuccessfully allied herself with Mark Antony and committed suicide, supposedly by an asp bite, in 30 BCE.
question.clue: The servant Eros was instructed to kill a lover of this ruler before that lover declared he was "grieved that a commander as great as I should be found to be inferior to a woman in courage."

swap.leadin: This structure is the burial place for the Pharaoh Khufu.
swap.text: Name this limestone structure, which is the only of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World still standing.
swap.answerHtml: The Great Pyramid of Giza (Or Great Pyramid of Khufu, or Pyramid of Cheops , prompt on pyramid or The Pyramids )
swap.clue: Slave labor was long thought to have been used to build this structure, but many archaeologists believe that thousands of skilled laborers were used instead over a 20 year period.

question.leadin: Antipater of Sidon listed one of this site's structures as one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
question.text: Name this site of the Great Pyramids, located just outside Cairo.
question.clue: The greatest wonders you beheld were the three pyramids of this city, the largest of which was built by the great pharaoh Khufu.

swap.text: Two answers required. These two portions of Ancient Egypt were united in the First Dynasty. They are represented by a red crown and a white crown.

question.leadin: In ancient Egypt, the vizier was the head official and top advisor in the pharaoh's court.
question.text: Perhaps the most significant early vizier was this man, who served under Djoser. Best known for his architectural work during his life, he was later deified as the god of medicine.
question.clue: The great Step Pyramid of Djoser at Saqqara is attributed to this minister and polymath, later deified as a god of medicine, who also completed projects abandoned by Sekhemkhet.

swap.leadin: Name some military leaders of the ancient Near East FTPE.
swap.text: A man by this name founded a kingdom in Egypt after Alexander's death. Many rulers sharing this name ruled Egypt for centuries afterwards.
swap.clue: A ruler of this name gathered seventy-two scholars to translate the Torah into Greek and commissioned a history of his kingdom from Manetho.

question.text: This pharaoh commanded the Egyptian forces at Kadesh. The temples at Abu Simbel were built during his reign.
question.clue: This son of Seti completed the hypostyle hall at Karnak, commissioned a giant statue of himself at Abu Simbel, and signed the world's first peace treaty with the Hittites following a huge chariot battle at Kadesh.

swap.text: After his conquest of Nubia, Ramesses built two temples near this site which display stone reliefs of him. Those temples at this site were covered by sand over time and rediscovered by Jean-Louis Burckhardt in 1813.
swap.clue: Four giant statues of Ramses are located in one of the temples at this location, where monuments were built in honor of the victory at Kadesh. Statues depicting Ramses as Osiris line the walls of the interior of that temple.

question.text: Aksumite rulers were known for constructing monuments of this type, consisting of tapered pillars with a pyramidal top. Many Egyptian monuments of this type, such as ones named "Lateran" and "Vatican," were installed in Rome under the Roman Empire.
question.clue: One of these structures built by Aksum was cut into three pieces for transport to Italy before being repatriated in 2005. A pair of these objects named for Cleopatra are found in London and New York City.

swap.leadin: CAN BE READ TO ANY TEAM This culture was conquered by the Hyksos ("HICK-sohs") from Western Asia, who set up a capital at Avaris.
swap.text: Name this culture that built pyramids along the Nile River.
swap.clue: This civilization was ruled from Amarna by the husband of Nefertiti.

question.text: Rome formed the province of Arabia Petraea after the death of a king with this epithet, Rabbel II. Ptolemy I also had this epithet which means "savior."
question.clue: Instead of being directly venerating kings as gods, Hellenistic ruler-cults often made offerings to the king under Greek title, which translates as "savior." It was given to the first ruler of the Ptolemaic dynasty.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Egypt's Hellenistic period.
swap.text: During the Hellenistic age, Egypt was ruled by a dynasty founded by this leader, one of the Macedonian generals who had conquered the Persian Empire.
swap.clue: He acquired his first wife Artacama during the mass wedding at Susa, cemented a later alliance by marrying Antipater's daughter Eurydice, and finally chose another wife, Berenice, to elevate to the title of queen.

question.text: The so-called "0 Dynasty" ends and the First Dynasty begins with Narmer unifying these two regions. The Narmer Palette found at Hierakonpolis shows him wearing the red and white crowns of these two regions.
question.answerHtml: Upper Egypt and Lower Egypt [accept Upper and Lower Egypt; accept the Sedge and the Bee]
question.clue: One of them had a name meaning "Land of the Reeds," the other was called the "Land of the North," and the two were collectively called Tawy("tah-wee").

swap.leadin: The Tomb of the Warriors in this man's mortuary temple is believed to contain the remains of warriors who died heroically as this king fought to reunify Egypt.
swap.text: Name this member of the 11th Dynasty and first pharaoh of the Middle Kingdom. This man's mortuary temple at Deir-el-Bahari, which contained a small pyramid at its top, inspired the neighboring one dedicated to Hatshepsut.

question.text: This first pharaoh of the Third Dynasty succeeded the mysterious Khasekhemwy. With the help of his vizier, Imhotep, he built the step pyramid at Saqqara.
question.clue: A legend that this ruler succeeded in stemming a 7-year drought by building a temple to Khnum at Elephantine can be found inscribed on the later Famine Stele.

swap.leadin: This pharaoh established a secure turquoise mining operation in Sinai, complete with fortifications to repel Bedouin invaders.
swap.text: Name this pharaoh who ordered the construction of the unfinished Black Pyramid and a trap-laden mortuary temple at Hawara, and is best-known for completing a canal to link the Nile with Lake Moeris in the al-Fayyum depression.
swap.clue: The greatest monarch of the Middle Kingdom, he built the mortuary complex known to Herodotus as the Labyrinth during his reign in the 19th century BC.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the end of the Old Kingdom, FTPE.
question.text: Toward the very end of the Old Kingdom, the Pyramid Texts began to be replaced by these religious texts, as exemplified by discoveries at the Balat necropolis. In general, they made the afterlife more accessible to commoners than the Pyramid Texts.

swap.leadin: Identify the following about monumental columns.
swap.text: Constructed of red Aswan granite, this Corinthian column, which despite its name was actually constructed by Diocletian to commemorate his defeat of the Alexandrian revolt, stands atop the former ground of the Serapeum.
